newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in London, rise in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in London, rise in Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - British shares closed lower as Wall Street's recent rally run ran out of steam while a press report sparked fears of an attack on tax breaks for pension funds in next month's British budget. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,745.1, down 38.0 points, or 0.79 percent.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trading at a record closing high, with the blue-chip DAX index lifted by a nearly 1 percent rise on Wall Street on Friday and the continued support of a firm dollar. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,765.11, up 20.67 points, or 0.55 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,750.02, down 2.35 points, or 0.06 percent.

PARIS - French stocks snapped a three-session winning streak after investors took profits on news of a long-awaited compromise deal by European Union leaders to keep the single currency project on track. The CAC-40 index closed at 2795.87, down 12.65 points, or 0.45 percent.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended easier in thin volume as recent gains were consolidated, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5,362.0, down 22.6 points, or 0.42 percent.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key index closed at a new high for calendar 1997, boosted by a last-minute spurt in the futures market. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,681.07, up 152.72 points, or 0.74 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended sharply higher, but brokers warned worries about the local property market could produce more volatility ahead. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,394.60, up 282.05 points, or 2.00 percent.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks closed at another record high with banks and insurers leading the charge as investors went chasing high yield stocks ahead of another expected local interest rate cut. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,669.3, up 14.0 points, or 0.53 percent.
JOHANNESBURG - The South African stock market was closed on Monday for a market holiday.
